citeAs: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth. Introducing EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Learning Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classification. In Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (IGARSS), 2018 IEEE International. IEEE, 2018.
creator: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth (TU Kaiserslautern, German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI))
description: A novel dataset based on Sentinel-2 satellite images covering 13 spectral bands and consisting of 10 classes with in total 27,000 labeled and geo-referenced images for land use and land cover classification.
name: EuroSAT
publisher: TU Kaiserslautern, German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI)
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: We manually checked all 27,000 images multiple times and corrected the ground truth by sorting out mislabeled images as well as images full of snow or ice.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: We manually checked all 27,000 images multiple times and corrected the ground truth by sorting out mislabeled images as well as images full of snow or ice.
rai:dataCollection: We gathered satellite images of European cities distributed in over 34 countries... We selected satellite images with a low cloud level... Based on the obtained satellite images, we created a dataset of 27,000 georeferenced and labeled image patches. The image patches measure 64x64 pixels and have been manually checked.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Satellite images taken by the satellite Sentinel-2A via Amazon S3. We chose satellite images associated with the cities covered in the European Urban Atlas.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Images recorded all over the year
rai:dataLimitations: The proposed dataset has not received atmospheric correction. This can result in images with a color cast.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Bands with a lower spatial resolution have been upsampled to 10 meters per pixel using cubic-spline interpolation.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The image patches measure 64x64 pixels... We manually checked all 27,000 images multiple times and corrected the ground truth by sorting out mislabeled images as well as images full of snow or ice.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The resulting classification system opens a gate towards a number of Earth observation applications. We demonstrate how this classification system can be used for detecting land use and land cover changes and how it can assist in improving geographical maps... deforestation is a main contributor to climate change, therefore the detection of deforested land is of particular interest.
rai:dataUseCases: Land use and land cover classification, detecting land use and land cover changes, assist in improving geographical maps.
